source: Terms used in project/paper.txt and project/README_*.md without a definition aimed at a general ML reader -- i.e. the 'curse of knowledge' the project's own materials carry. These become the term-ledger's must-define list for audience mode B (adjacent researcher).
assumed_known_by_project_materials_but_n: resolve rate (SWE-Bench's pass/fail metric for whether a patch makes the hidden tests pass)
0-shot vs 1-shot (in the sense of a demonstration trajectory given to an agent, not just an ICL example)
CodeAct (treating code execution itself as the action space)
hint text (SWE-Bench-specific: optional natural-language suggestions bundled with a task)
GitHub issue / GitHub pull request as a unit of software-engineering work
specific benchmark identities and what each one actually measures (SWE-Bench, HumanEvalFix, WebArena, MiniWoB++, GAIA, GPQA, AgentBench, MINT, ProofWriter, Entity Deduction Arena)
assumed_known_by_mode_B_reader_already: supervised/instruction-tuned large language models (GPT-4, Claude, etc.)
prompting, zero-shot/few-shot inference in the general ICL sense
standard statistics: percentages, comparison against baselines
general notion of a benchmark suite and a leaderboard-style comparison table
the general concept of an 'AI agent' that takes actions in an environment (from RL or general agents literature), without subfield-specific tooling
implication_for_draft: Every term in the first list must be defined in one clause at first use (term ledger), and every benchmark named in the Results section needs a one-clause description of the task it measures before its number is reported.
